prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1389; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the intersection in Pasadena, Texas, I found a rear-end collision involving two vehicles. Driver 1 was seated in the rear-impacted vehicle and reported pain in the left wrist. Driver 2 stated that the other vehicle slowed briefly and was struck from behind as Driver 2 was stopped in traffic. The damage to both vehicles is consistent with that impact, with crush concentrated at the rear of the first vehicle and the front of the second. The reported wrist injury is consistent with the force of a collision of this type. Driver 1 was identified at the scene and a passing motorist confirmed seeing Driver 1 and a Passenger inside the vehicle after the impact. No independent witness to the collision itself was located, and no photographs or other incident reports were submitted by any party. I found no indication of prior damage to the vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as the named driver on the insurance record for that vehicle. Both vehicles were moved to the shoulder, and Driver 1 was transported for evaluation.
